subject: Planned: Sequenced runtime refresh in us-east3 — minimal impact window
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@optihealth.com>, acct-eng@optihealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 15:00:00 +0000
Subject: Planned: Sequenced runtime refresh in us-east3 — minimal impact window

Hi Sara / OptiHealth team,

Heads-up: we have a short, sequenced runtime maintenance window scheduled for the us-east3 region on Wednesday, 2027-08-04 between 02:00–04:00 UTC. This is a targeted kernel/driver refresh across a subset of inference pools to address a latency regression we observed under specific long-sequence workloads.

What to expect
- We will perform rolling restarts of small node groups to apply the driver patch; each group will be drained and restarted independently to keep most capacity available.
- Typical request routing will maintain availability; you may see isolated 20–60s tail latency spikes for a small percentage of requests during the drain of the node serving that request.
- No customer data will be moved outside your region; KV cache warmup is preserved where possible (see attached matrix).

Mitigations we have in place
- Canary run completed on non-production pools with no loss of cached state.
- Smart routing will retry failed requests automatically and fall back to nearest compatible model variant in the rare event of a service interruption.
- Our on-call SRE team will monitor telemetry and can pause the rolling ahead of schedule if we observe customer impact.

Requested action from you
- If you have scheduled heavy batch jobs or latency-sensitive runs hitting us-east3 during the window, please either reschedule or let us know and we can coordinate a targeted exclusion.
- Reply with any blackout periods we should avoid.

Attachments: sequenced-runtime-refresh-ops-plan.pdf, kv-cache-persistence-matrix.csv

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Redwood Inference

Looping in a couple of operational notes so the customer has clear points of contact and escalation.

Operational notes for the run
- We will run groups in 10–12 minute windows: 5 min drain, 3–6 min restart/healthcheck before traffic resumes.
- Primary on-call: Monica (SRE) — +1 (212) 555-0112, secondary: Stephanie (Infra).
- Post-run validation: we'll run a synthetic latency sweep (10k requests) and share a quick dashboard snapshot within 30 minutes of completion.

I'll also include the doc link to the rollback checklist in the Drive file we attached.

-Monica
Monica Patel

From: Sara Lim <sara@optihealth.com>

Cc: acct-eng@optihealth.com, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 08:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Planned: Sequenced runtime refresh in us-east3 — minimal impact window

Thanks for the notice — appreciate the details. A couple quick questions from our engineering team:

1) KV cache persistence: our real-time comparator relies on warm KV caches. If a node is restarted and the cache is lost, is there an automatic pre-warm against a warmed snapshot or will we see a cold-cache penalty for affected tokens?
2) Can you confirm whether model variant failover is per-request or session-bound? Our session affinity could be affected.

We don't have blackout windows during that UTC period but we do have a scheduled nightly sync at 03:20 UTC which could be sensitive to transient latency. If you expect any spiky behavior around that time, we may shift that job.

-Sara
Sara Lim
Head of Platform, OptiHealth
sara@optihealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@optihealth.com>, acct-eng@optihealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Planned: Sequenced runtime refresh in us-east3 — minimal impact window

Thanks Sara — good questions, answered inline below.

1) KV cache persistence: for this refresh we preserve KV cache where the node is not drained. For groups we do fully drain, there will be cold-cache behavior on first requests. We mitigate by:
- prioritizing warmup on replicas behind the same routing domain before promoting them to production traffic,
- proactively pre-warming the most commonly-requested prefixes using a lightweight background traffic generator immediately after the node health check passes.
See the attached kv-cache-persistence-matrix.csv for expected warmup timings by model/sequence length.

2) Model variant failover: failover is per-request. We do not change session affinity for active websocket sessions; HTTP request routing will retry and may be served by the closest compatible variant only for new attempts. If your workflow requires strict session affinity through the window, let us know and we can apply a temporary no-route override for your tenancy.

Regarding your 03:20 UTC nightly sync — that time overlaps with the middle of our window. If you can shift that job by 40 minutes we recommend doing so. If not, flag it here and we'll mark OptiHealth as a near-zero-tolerance tenant and coordinate a brief exclusion during the sync.

Postmortem / follow-up
- We'll circulate a short post-run summary (timeline, observed metrics, any anomalies, and remediation) within 24 hours.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute sync the day after to walk through the postmortem with your infra team.

Let me know how you'd like us to treat the 03:20 job and if you'd like the follow-up sync.

Best,
Rishi
